summary: Issue-tracker pack built as one generic transport plus one methodology tool, deliberately not as a per-vendor client: every SaaS API breaks eventually and a shipped client that 500s on a customer's machine costs more trust than a missing feature. api-call.py is the only networking code — a declarative profile per vendor (base URL, auth header shape, pagination by page, cursor or Link header, named operations) and a --select path expression that shapes the response down to the fields the caller named, so a list of 40 issues costs 40 short rows instead of 40 vendor envelopes. That compression is the justification for duplicating something the vendors already ship: ClickUp's official MCP server is capped at 50 calls per 24 hours on Free against roughly 144,000 a day for the REST API, and every call it does answer bills the model for the whole envelope. It is dry-run until --yes, honours Retry-After on a 429, and exits 3 on an absent credential, 4 on a rejected one and 6 on a vendor error, so a calling agent can tell 'you have no credential' from 'I crashed'. sdd-sync.py reconciles a feature's SDD task files — the todo/, in-progress/, done/ directory-as-status lifecycle — against a tracker snapshot through a hash ledger that persists task file to remote id to last hash. The ledger is the point: without it a second run creates the whole task set again, every time, and it is also what lets the tool report local-ahead, remote-ahead and conflict rather than silently picking a winner. A conflict exits 1 and touches nothing; a plan the caller never executed is reported rather than recorded as synced. Ships profiles for GitHub Issues, Linear and ClickUp v2.

credentials.min_scope: The pack-level fallback, used only when the per-profile variable is unset; prefer GITHUB_TOKEN, LINEAR_API_KEY or CLICKUP_TOKEN so one credential cannot reach three vendors. Least privilege per vendor: a GitHub fine-grained token scoped to the one repository with Issues read, plus Issues write only for a push; a Linear personal API key on a workspace whose membership is the scope, sent with no Bearer prefix; a ClickUp personal token, also unprefixed, on an account that can see only the target list. No admin, org or billing scope of any kind, and no delete permission, because no operation in this pack issues a DELETE.
